title: The kelvin is fixed by setting k to 1.380649×10^−23 J/K
summary: NIST defines the kelvin by fixing the Boltzmann constant. The 2022 CODATA row marks that value exact.
body: NIST's temperature page says the kelvin is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Boltzmann constant k to be 1.380 649 × 10^{−23} when expressed in J K^{−1}. The BIPM defining-constants table prints the same k as 1.380 649 × 10^{−23} J/K. The 2022 CODATA listing marks the Boltzmann constant exact. NIST's page also says that 0 K is commonly called absolute zero, that one Celsius degree is an interval of 1 K, and that zero degrees Celsius is 273.15 K.
